slides.title: Process mapping pilot
slides.lead: Client A chooses the process to map and the outputs it wants. Over a few weeks, Source gathers the evidence, builds the maps and reviews them with your nominated expert.
slides.support: A short pilot within Client A’s own operations, with practical findings and direct experience of the method.

slides.title: Where Client A is today
slides.lead: What we understand so far from the material Client A has shared. Each point names its source.

points.heading: The work crosses several teams
points.text: The process runs across [N] teams, and hand-overs between them happen by email and shared spreadsheets.

points.heading: Most steps are not written down
points.text: The process overview covers the main stages, but not who does each step or which system it uses.

points.heading: Volumes are growing
points.text: The team expects the current way of working to come under pressure as volumes grow.
points.to_confirm: Confirm current and expected volumes with the process owner

implication.text: A clear, shared map of how the work really runs comes before deciding what to change or automate.

slides.title: How the pilot would work
slides.subtitle: What we would look at, what you would receive, and what it takes from both sides.

slides.title: Choose the focus
slides.lead: Pick one area for the pilot. Each option is small enough to map in a few weeks and large enough to show results.

options.title: Order to cash
options.text: From a customer’s order to cash received, including credit checks and invoicing.
questions: Where do orders wait, and why?
Which steps are re-keyed by hand?

evidence.text: Named in the first call as the main pain point.

options.title: Month-end close
options.text: The tasks, reconciliations and sign-offs that close each month.
questions: Which tasks hold up the close?
Where are checks done by hand?

options.title: Supplier onboarding
options.text: Setting up a new supplier, from the first request to the first payment.

slides.note: Or another area Client A would like to explore.

slides.title: What you could receive

slides.title: From scope to results in four weeks
slides.lead: Four steps, with your expert reviewer involved throughout.

steps.title: Set the scope
steps.text: Confirm the focus, the outputs, the expert reviewer and the people we will speak to.

steps.title: Gather the evidence
steps.text: Short interviews, screen recordings of key steps and the documents you share.

steps.title: Build the maps
steps.text: We draft the maps and outputs, then check them with your expert.

steps.title: Share the results
steps.text: Present the findings on-site or online, discuss open questions and agree next steps.

slides.total: About four weeks in all, depending on how quickly the interviews can be booked.

slides.title: Two roles and a few documents
slides.lead: Both roles come from within Client A’s team. We keep the time asked of them small.

items.text: Someone who knows the chosen area and can review our outputs, challenge the findings and guide the recommendations.
People who do the work and can explain it through short interviews, screen recordings and follow-up questions.
Process notes, templates and examples that show how the work is done today.

slides.note: We will agree the documents and examples needed when we set the scope.

slides.title: A small team, from scope to results
slides.lead: The same people stay with the pilot throughout, with partner firms where they add depth.
